generation.explanation: A cone and a cylinder with the same base radius R and height H have cross-sectional areas that behave very differently. The cylinder’s slice is always πR², while the cone’s radius shrinks linearly from the base, so its slice area shrinks as the square of the remaining height. Integrating those areas from base to tip gives V_cone = ∫ πR²(h/H)² dh = (1/3)πR²H — exactly one-third the cylinder’s volume.
